mainTopic: Whether an owner can redeem or give up produce that is no longer in his possession: ברירה, רבי יוחנן's sources, and how the צנועין relate to רבי דוסא
overview: This amud keeps asking whether the צנועין, who redeemed fruit after passersby had taken it, fit with רבי יוחנן's rule that you cannot make holy something that is not in your possession. First a משנה about wine bought from כותים shows that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה. Then the גמרא objects that flipping the ברייתא and reading it as 'whatever will be picked' only moves the contradiction onto רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן also rejects ברירה, as we see from his ruling that brothers who divide an inheritance count as buyers. So the גמרא goes back to 'whatever was picked.' It explains that רבי יוחנן followed a different unattributed משנה: one who steals from a thief pays no כפל, because a stolen item is fully in neither person's control. A פסוק about making one's house holy supports that משנה over the צנועין. Then אביי, רבא and רבינא each say how they would have understood the צנועין and רבי דוסא if רבי יוחנן had not said that the two hold the same view. רבא links the צנועין to רבי מאיר through a גזירה שוה between כרם רבעי and מעשר שני. רבינא's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wine of the כותים: proof that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. רבי מאיר lets a buyer declare which portions he will later separate as תרומה and מעשרות and drink right away. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who buys wine from the כותים says: 'Two לוגין that I will separate later are תרומה, ten are מעשר ראשון, nine are מעשר שני.' He redeems the מעשר שני and drinks at once. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove its earlier point that רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's method only works with ברירה: when the buyer drinks, nobody yet knows which wine is the תרומה and מעשרות. The separation is treated as if it took effect back at the moment of the declaration. Since רבי יהודה forbids this, he does not accept ברירה. That makes it hard to say he holds the morning declaration of 'whatever will be picked.'

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans; people suspected of not separating תרומה and tithes properly
A liquid measure
The portion given to a כהן
First tithe (given to a לוי) and second tithe (eaten in ירושלים or redeemed with money)
Redeems; moves the holiness of מעשר שני onto coins
They forbid

steps.confusionAlert: The word ברירה never appears in this משנה. The גמרא assumes the reason the three חכמים forbid is that they reject ברירה.

phrases.english: One who buys wine from among the Kutim

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי לוּגִּין שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ –
phrases.english: says: Two log that I will separate in the future
are hereby teruma;
ten are first tithe;
nine are second tithe;
and he redeems and drinks immediately,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹסְרִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Shimon forbid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the objection, raised just before this section, that רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about wine bought from כותים, where רבי יהודה forbids relying on a future separation.

steps.title: Reversing the ברייתא just moves the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was gained by reversing the ברייתא. It fixed a contradiction in רבי יהודה, but it creates a new contradiction in רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: In the end, why did you reverse the teaching? Because רבי יהודה seemed to contradict himself. But now רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole idea of reversing the ברייתא. It says the reversal does not really solve anything, and the next step explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the reversal was to keep רבי יהודה consistent. The גמרא now says the price is a new contradiction, this time in רבי יוחנן. A fix that only shifts the problem to someone else is not a real fix.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; when all is said and done
You reversed (switched the opinions)
There is a contradiction between one statement of a sage and another of his
Now too

phrases.english: They said: In the end,
why are you reversing the teaching?
phrases.notes: Here מתניתין means the ברייתא with רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא, which was flipped earlier to fit רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה;
phrases.english: Because of the contradiction between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda;
now too
there is a contradiction between Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yoḥanan,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: סוֹף סוֹף, אַמַּאי קָא אָפְכַתְּ לַהּ לְמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the proof about רבי יהודה and attacks the reversal approach as a whole.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier proposal to reverse the ברייתא (and reread it as 'כל המתלקט') on רבי יוחנן's behalf.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reversal was meant to remove a self-contradiction in רבי יהודה. Instead it creates one in רבי יוחנן, so nothing is gained.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן now contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: Changing the wording to 'whatever will be picked' means רבי יוחנן accepts ברירה. But it is known that רבי יוחנן does not accept ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said, according to רבי יוחנן: Don't say 'whatever was picked,' say 'whatever will be picked.' So he accepts ברירה. But רבי יוחנן does not accept ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the contradiction in רבי יוחנן that it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Whatever was picked' looks back at fruit already taken, so no ברירה is needed. 'Whatever will be picked' looks forward: which fruit is redeemed only becomes clear later, which is ברירה. Since רבי יוחנן is known to reject ברירה, the reading proposed on his behalf clashes with his known position.

keyTerms.meaning: What was picked (already happened)
What will be picked (in the future)
Apparently; this shows that
Retroactive designation: a later choice shows what was meant from the start
He holds / he does not hold

steps.whatToRemember: The reversal saved רבי יהודה from contradicting himself. But the new wording 'כל המתלקט' depends on ברירה, which רבי יוחנן rejects, so now רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the one-word difference: נלקט is the past ('was picked'), and מתלקט is the future ('will be picked'). Only the future version needs ברירה.

phrases.english: For you said, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Do not say "whatever was picked,"
rather say "whatever will be picked"
apparently he holds of retroactive designation;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֵית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה,
phrases.english: but Rabbi Yoḥanan does not hold of retroactive designation!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרַתְּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא תֵּימָא כׇּל הַנִּלְקָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the contradiction in רבי יוחנן announced in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rereading of the declaration as 'כל המתלקט.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forward-looking declaration requires ברירה, yet רבי יוחנן is known to reject ברירה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יוחנן does not accept ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's ruling that brothers who split an inheritance count as buyers. This proves he does not accept ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: brothers who divided an inheritance count as buyers from each other, and they return the land to each other in the יובל year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from step 3. It shows where we know that רבי יוחנן does not accept ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ברירה worked, we would say each brother's share was his from the moment the father died. רבי יוחנן says instead that each brother 'bought' his share from the others, so it goes back at יובל like any sold field. That means he does not accept ברירה, so the new wording 'whatever will be picked' cannot fit his view.

keyTerms.meaning: The idea that a later choice shows what was already true from the start
Buyers
The Jubilee year, when sold fields go back to their original owners
Brothers who divided an inheritance

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Brothers who divided [an inheritance] are buyers,
and they return [the land] to each other in the Jubilee year!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind step 3's claim that רבי יוחנן does not accept ברירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that brothers who divide an inheritance are buyers and return the land at יובל

steps.title: Going back to the wording 'whatever was picked'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the change in wording and says the צנועין really said 'whatever was picked.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really the wording is 'whatever was picked.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs off from its earlier change in wording. This also sets up the next question: if so, why did רבי יוחנן disagree with the צנועין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the past-tense wording, the redemption happens after the grapes were already stolen, so ברירה plays no role at all. But now we need a new reason why רבי יוחנן rejected the צנועין, and the next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, really; drops an earlier suggestion and goes back to the original
Whatever was picked (past tense)

phrases.english: Rather, really [the wording is] "whatever was picked,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the proof in step 4 by dropping the 'will be picked' wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction of the earlier change in wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גמרא, defending רבי יוחנן, had changed the wording to 'whatever will be picked,' which would depend on ברירה
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording is 'whatever was picked,' so ברירה is not the issue

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's real source: stealing from a thief
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן relied on a different unattributed משנה: a person who steals from a thief pays no כפל. The גמרא asks why he does not pay the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן found another unattributed משנה, as we learned: one who steals from a thief does not pay double. Why? We understand why he does not pay the first thief, because the פסוק says 'stolen from the house of the man,' and not from the house of a thief. But he should pay the owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן rejected the צנועין: he had another משנה that points the other way. Then it asks a question about that משנה, which sets up the conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that the second thief pays כפל to no one. Not paying the first thief makes sense from the פסוק. Not paying the owner is puzzling, and that puzzle is the key to רבי יוחנן's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed משנה, which usually sets the halacha
The double payment a thief owes
Why?
Granted, this part makes sense

steps.confusionAlert: The second thief pays no כפל to the first thief and also none to the original owner. The question here is only about the owner.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan found a different unattributed [משנה],
as we learned:
One who steals after a thief does not
pay the double payment.
Why?
Granted, to the first thief he does not pay,
[because it says] "and it is stolen from the house of the man,"
and not from the house of the thief;
but to the owner, let him pay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reason for רבי יוחנן's view now that ברירה is no longer the explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for רבי יוחנן's position
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן based his view on the משנה about one who steals from a thief

steps.title: A stolen item is fully in neither person's control
steps.stepSummary: The thief does not own the item, and the owner does not have it. So neither one can make it הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this: this one, because it is not his, and that one, because it is not in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question and explains רבי יוחנן's reasoning. A stolen item is not fully under anyone's control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first thief has the item but does not own it. The owner owns it but does not have it. Since the owner lacks possession, he cannot make it הקדש after it is stolen, which explains why רבי יוחנן disagreed with the חסידים.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude
It is not his; he does not own it
In his possession or control

steps.whatToRemember: A stolen item is in a 'no one's control' state: the thief does not own it, and the owner does not hold it. This is רבי יוחנן's reason, not ברירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea about stolen items explains why an owner cannot make his stolen property הקדש. It replaces the ברירה explanation the גמרא tried earlier.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
this one, because it is not his,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the first thief: he holds the item but does not own it.

phrases.english: and that one, because it is not in his possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why not pay the owner' question from step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A stolen item is fully in the control of neither the owner (he does not have it) nor the thief (he does not own it), so the owner cannot make it הקדש after the theft.

steps.title: Why follow that unattributed משנה and not the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's choice. Why did he follow the unattributed משנה about the thief rather than the unattributed משנה of the צנועין?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made him follow that unattributed משנה? Let him rule like this unattributed משנה of the צנועין!
steps.whatsHappening: There are two unattributed משניות that seem to disagree. The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן picked the one about the thief over the one about the צנועין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, רבי יוחנן relied on the משנה about stealing from a thief. That משנה teaches that a stolen item is not in the owner's possession. But the צנועין משנה suggests that the owner can still act on produce that has been taken. The גמרא wants a reason for preferring one unattributed משנה over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? This asks for the reason behind a choice.
An unattributed משנה, stated without naming who said it.
The pious ones mentioned in the earlier משנה.
Let him act, meaning let him rule this way.

phrases.english: And what did you see
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter in round brackets. Either way it means 'what did you see,' asking for a reason.

phrases.english: that he follows that unattributed משנה?
Let him act according to this unattributed משנה of the pious ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חָזֵית דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר הַהִיא סְתָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source that רבי יוחנן relied on in Steps 6-7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's choice to follow the unattributed משנה about the thief.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are two unattributed משניות that point in opposite directions, and nothing yet explains why one should win over the other.

steps.title: A פסוק supports the משנה about the thief
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן followed that משנה because a פסוק supports it: just as a person's house is in his possession, so too anything he makes holy must be in his possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a פסוק supports it: 'And when a man shall make his house holy to ה׳.' Just as his house is in his possession, so too everything he makes holy must be in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. The משנה about the thief has a פסוק backing it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a man making his house holy. A house is something he owns and holds. From this we learn that a person can only make something holy if it is in his possession. A stolen item is not in his possession, so this fits the משנה about the thief, and that gives it the stronger standing.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק supports it.
He will make holy, meaning he dedicates it to the בית המקדש.
In his possession or domain.

steps.whatToRemember: You can only make something הקדש if it is in your possession, just like 'his house.' This פסוק is why רבי יוחנן prefers the משנה about the thief.

phrases.english: Because a verse supports it:
"And when a man shall make his house holy
to be holy to ה׳"
just as his house is in his possession,
so too everything must be in his possession.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Support from a פסוק breaks the tie between the two unattributed משניות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two unattributed משניות are equally strong, so there is no reason to prefer one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה about the thief is supported by a פסוק that requires an item to be in one's possession in order to make it holy.

steps.title: אביי: Without רבי יוחנן, the two views would only partly match
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that if רבי יוחנן had not said the צנועין and רבי דוסא hold the same thing, he would have said the צנועין agree with רבי דוסא, but רבי דוסא does not agree with the צנועין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If רבי יוחנן had not said that the צנועין and רבי דוסא said the same thing, I would have said that the צנועין hold like רבי דוסא, but רבי דוסא does not hold like the צנועין.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his own view of how the צנועין and רבי דוסא relate to each other. This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the two opinions are identical. אביי says that on his own he would have seen the agreement as going only one way. The צנועין's view would include רבי דוסא's view, but not the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for.
One thing, meaning the same ruling.
I would have said.
They hold of it / he does not hold of it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Abaye said: If not for what Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: צְנוּעִין, וְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: that the pious ones and Rabbi Dosa said the same thing,
I would have said:
the pious ones hold the view of Rabbi Dosa,
but Rabbi Dosa does not hold the view of the pious ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement by אביי about how the צנועין and רבי דוסא compare.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without רבי יוחנן's statement, the agreement would go only one way: the צנועין would accept רבי דוסא's view, but רבי דוסא would not accept theirs.

steps.title: אביי explains: an ordinance for a thief versus one for poor people
steps.stepSummary: The צנועין made an ordinance even for a thief, so they would surely make one for poor people. But רבי דוסא made it only for poor people, not for a thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: The צנועין hold like רבי דוסא: if the רבנן made an ordinance for a thief, do we need to say they would do so for poor people? But רבי דוסא does not hold like the צנועין: the רבנן made an ordinance for poor people, but they did not make one for a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the reasoning behind his one-way comparison from Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צנועין helped even a thief, who does not deserve help, so they would surely help innocent poor people. That is why their view includes רבי דוסא's view. רבי דוסא only spoke about poor people, so we cannot assume he would also help a thief.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinance, a rule the רבנן set up to help people.
A thief.
Poor people.
Does it need to be said? Meaning it is obvious.

steps.whatToRemember: This works like a קל וחומר in one direction only. Helping a thief tells you that you would help the poor, but helping the poor does not tell you that you would help a thief.

phrases.english: The pious ones hold the view of Rabbi Dosa:
if for a thief the Rabbis made an ordinance,
for poor people, does it need to be said?
Rabbi Dosa does not hold the view of the pious ones:

phrases.aramaic: עֲנִיִּים הוּא דַּעֲבַדוּ לְהוּ רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא,
phrases.english: it is for poor people that the Rabbis made an ordinance,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גַּנָּב לָא עֲבַדוּ לַיהּ רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא.
phrases.english: but for a thief the Rabbis did not make an ordinance.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְנוּעִין אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי דּוֹסָא וּמָה בְּגַנָּב עֲבַדוּ רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind אביי's statement in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinance made for a thief implies one for poor people, but an ordinance made for poor people does not imply one for a thief.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without רבי יוחנן's statement, the צנועין's view would include רבי דוסא's view, but not the reverse.

steps.title: רבא would have tied the pious ones to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if not for רבי יוחנן, he would have said the צנועין's ruling follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If רבי יוחנן had not said that the צנועין and רבי דוסא hold the same thing, I would have said: Who taught the ruling of the צנועין? It is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new statement, much like אביי's in Step 10. He names the תנא he would have connected to the צנועין. The next lines explain his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had said that the צנועין and רבי דוסא share one idea. רבא says that without this, he would have given the צנועין a separate source: רבי מאיר. That would let the צנועין rest on a reason that does not apply to רבי דוסא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: The pious ones, who made an ordinance about כרם רבעי fruit
I would have said (an idea that turns out not to be the final view)
Who is the תנא who taught this?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rava said: If not for the fact that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: צְנוּעִין וְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: the pious ones and Rabbi Dosa said the same thing,
I would have said:
Who is the tanna who taught the pious ones' ruling?
It is Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels אביי's statement with a different way to separate the צנועין from רבי דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without רבי יוחנן's statement, the צנועין would be attributed to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: For redemption the Torah treats the tithe as his
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds מעשר belongs to Heaven, yet the Torah calls it "his tithe" for פדיון and makes him add a fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי מאיר say that tithe is Heaven's property? Even so, for redemption the Torah treats it as his, as it is written: "And if a man will redeem any of his tithe, he shall add its fifth to it." The Torah calls it "his tithe," and he adds a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his basis for linking the צנועין to רבי מאיר. Even though רבי מאיר says מעשר is not really the person's, the פסוק still calls it "his" for פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that, for פדיון, real ownership is not needed. The Torah can treat something as "his" even when it belongs to גבוה. This idea becomes useful in the next step for כרם רבעי.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני, the second tithe
Property of the Most High, belonging to Heaven
Redemption, moving the holiness onto money
An added fifth, which the owner pays when redeeming his own מעשר

phrases.english: Doesn't Rabbi Meir say:
tithe is property of the Most High,
phrases.notes: He means the second tithe, the one a person brings to ירושלים or redeems with money.

phrases.english: and even so, regarding redemption,
the Merciful One established it in his possession?
As it is written:
"And if a man will redeem any of his tithe,
he shall add its fifth to it" –
the Merciful One called it "his tithe,"
and so he adds a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reasoning behind רבא's link to רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: Something can be treated as a person's for פדיון even when it is ממון גבוה.

steps.title: Fourth-year vineyard learns from tithe
steps.stepSummary: Through a גזירה שוה of the word "קדש", כרם רבעי takes on the rules of מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fourth-year vineyard as well: it learns "holy" and "holy" from tithe. It is written here: "Holy, for giving praise," and it is written regarding tithe: "And all the tithe of the land, of the seed of the land, of the fruit of the tree, is the Lord's; it is holy."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא carries the מעשר rule over to כרם רבעי, which is the case the צנועין dealt with. He does this through a matching word, "קדש", that appears in both topics.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since כרם רבעי is learned from מעשר, the owner is treated as "his" for פדיון of כרם רבעי too, even if he does not truly own it. This is how רבא would explain the צנועין redeeming fruit even after a thief took it. The rest of רבא's argument continues after this.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a vineyard in its fourth year, which is holy and is eaten in ירושלים or redeemed
Learns, here by a matching-word comparison
A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places
Holy, for giving praise (the phrase used for fourth-year fruit)

phrases.english: A fourth-year vineyard as well –
it learns "holy" and "holy" from tithe,
phrases.notes: The same word "holy" appears in both topics, so the rules of one carry over to the other.

phrases.english: it is written here: "Holy, for giving praise,"
and it is written regarding tithe:
"And all the tithe of the land,
whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the tree,
is the Lord's; it is holy."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the מעשר rule from Step 13 to כרם רבעי, the case of the צנועין.
steps.raayaObject: כרם רבעי shares מעשר's rules, including being treated as the owner's for פדיון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה of "קדש" from ויקרא 19:24 and ויקרא 27:30

steps.title: Applying the 'holy' comparison: the owner controls desacralizing
steps.stepSummary: Just as מעשר שני belongs to Heaven yet the owner redeems it, so too כרם רבעי belongs to Heaven yet the owner desacralizes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as 'holy' written by מעשר means that, even though it is Heaven's property, the Torah left it in the owner's control for redemption, so too 'holy' written by כרם רבעי means that, even though it is not his own property, the Torah left it in his control for desacralizing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what the גזירה שוה from the last step teaches. Whatever is true of מעשר שני is carried over to כרם רבעי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, מעשר שני is ממון גבוה, which means Heaven's property, and yet the Torah lets the owner redeem it. The word 'קדש' links כרם רבעי to it. So כרם רבעי is also Heaven's property that the owner may desacralize.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that belongs to Heaven, not to a person
Redemption, moving holiness onto money
To desacralize, to make holy produce ordinary
The Torah placed it in his control
Fruit of a vineyard in its fourth year, which is holy

phrases.english: Just as 'holy' that is written regarding tithe —
phrases.notes: This means מעשר שני, the second tithe, which רבי מאיר holds belongs to Heaven.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ הוּא,
phrases.english: even though it is property of the Most High,
regarding redemption the Merciful One placed it in his control;

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַאי ״קֹדֶשׁ״ נָמֵי דִּכְתִיב גַּבֵּי כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי –
phrases.english: so too this 'holy' written regarding the fourth-year vineyard —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו מָמוֹן דִּידֵיהּ הוּא,
phrases.english: even though it is not his own property,
regarding desacralizing the Merciful One placed it in his control;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the content of the גזירה שוה introduced in step 14
steps.raayaObject: The owner of כרם רבעי may desacralize fruit that belongs to Heaven
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גזירה שוה of 'קדש' linking כרם רבעי to מעשר שני, which רבי מאיר holds is ממון גבוה

steps.title: So desacralizing after a theft is nothing new
steps.stepSummary: Even when the fruit sits in his possession it is not his, and he can still desacralize it. That is why he can do so after a thief took it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For even when it is in his possession, it is not his, and yet he can desacralize it. That is why he can desacralize it even when it is stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion that explains the צנועין's ordinance according to רבי מאיר. Desacralizing stolen fruit is not a special new power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner never 'owned' the holy fruit in the first place, yet he always desacralizes it. So whether the fruit is in his house or with a thief makes no difference. The thief taking it changes nothing about his power.

keyTerms.meaning: He is able to desacralize
It is in his possession

phrases.english: For even when it is in his possession —
it is not his,
and yet he can desacralize it;
because of this he can desacralize it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from the comparison in step 15
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי מאיר, desacralizing כרם רבעי after it was stolen is no bigger a power than desacralizing it normally.

steps.title: Gleanings are different because they are truly his
steps.stepSummary: With the poor people's gleanings, the sheaves belong to the owner. So he may only be able to make them ownerless while he still has them, not after they were taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with לקט, since it is his own property, he can make it ownerless when it is in his possession. When it is not in his possession, he cannot make it ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא contrasts the case of רבי דוסא with the צנועין. He shows why agreeing with the צנועין does not force anyone to agree with רבי דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making something ownerless (הפקר) is a power an owner has over his own things, and maybe only while he holds them. The holy fruit was never the owner's, so possession never mattered there. That is why, according to רבא, the צנועין would not have to agree with רבי דוסא.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleanings; here, the sheaves the poor took by mistake
Make ownerless (הפקר)
It is not in his possession

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes רבא's picture. If not for רבי יוחנן, the צנועין would follow רבי מאיר and would not have to agree with רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: But regarding gleanings —
since it is his own property,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִיתֵיהּ בִּרְשׁוּתֵיהּ הוּא דְּמָצֵי מַפְקַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: it is when it is in his possession that he can make it ownerless,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֵיתֵיהּ בִּרְשׁוּתֵיהּ לָא מָצֵי מַפְקַר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: when it is not in his possession he cannot make it ownerless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts רבי דוסא's case with the צנועין case explained in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An owner may only be able to make his own property ownerless while it is in his possession, so the צנועין's ruling does not prove רבי דוסא's.

steps.title: רבינא: I would have said the צנועין are רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that if not for רבי יוחנן, he would have identified the צנועין as רבי דוסא. He would do this to save רבי יוחנן from a difficulty with an unattributed משנה. The גמרא then starts to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: If רבי יוחנן had not said that the צנועין and רבי דוסא said the same thing, I would have said: who is the תנא of the צנועין? It is רבי דוסא. That way a סתם משנה would not be difficult for רבי יוחנן. And רבי יוחנן —
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא, רבינא, gives his own 'if not for רבי יוחנן' statement, like אביי and רבא did before him. The last words, 'and רבי יוחנן', set up an explanation that continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא each said they would have separated the צנועין from רבי דוסא. רבינא goes the other way and would have said they are the very same תנא. His reason is to keep a סתם משנה from contradicting רבי יוחנן, and the גמרא is about to explain why that matters to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed משנה, with no name given
Who is the תנא (the author)?
The same thing, the same view
It would be difficult for, it would contradict

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not disagreeing with רבי יוחנן. Like אביי and רבא, he only says what he would have thought if רבי יוחנן had not spoken.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
If Rabbi Yoḥanan had not said

phrases.aramaic: צְנוּעִין וְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: the pious ones and Rabbi Dosa said the same thing,
I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תַּנָּא צְנוּעִין – רַבִּי דּוֹסָא הִיא,
phrases.english: who taught the pious ones? It is Rabbi Dosa,
so that it should not be difficult —
an unattributed mishna, for Rabbi Yoḥanan.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי and רבא, a third אמורא offers his own 'if not for רבי יוחנן' reading, this time joining the צנועין to רבי דוסא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without רבי יוחנן's statement, רבינא would have said that the צנועין's view is רבי דוסא's, so that a סתם משנה would not contradict רבי יוחנן.
